samples.text:
The maps show Hollin Farm in 2005 and the same place in 2024 when it became an eco-park. Overall, the farming land and buildings was changed for visitors and nature, but the roads, the stream, the farmhouse and the trees are the same.

In 2005, the farmhouse was in the north of the farm next to Country Road, and there was a barn and a cattle shed to the east of it. There was a wheat field in the west and a grazing land in the east, and a stream in the south. There were also trees in the north-west.

In 2024, the wheat field has been changed to a wildflower meadow and a pond was made next to it, with a bird hide near the pond. The grazing land is now a camping area. Also the barn became a visitor centre and the cattle shed became toilets and showers. A car park has been build near to the trees in the north-west. In addition, there is a nature trail that go around the meadow and the camping area.
samples.why: Overview present · key changes covered with limited detail on positions · simple linking · adequate vocabulary · several errors in agreement, articles and verb forms that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The maps illustrate how Hollin Farm was converted into an eco-park between 2005 and 2024. Overall, the agricultural land and farm buildings have been adapted for leisure and wildlife, whereas the basic layout, including the farmhouse, the roads, the stream and the trees, has been preserved.

In 2005, the farmhouse stood in the north of the site, connected to Country Road by a short road, with a barn and a cattle shed to its east. The land to the south was used for farming, with a wheat field in the west and grazing land in the east, and a stream flowed along the southern edge.

By 2024, the barn had been turned into a visitor centre and the cattle shed into toilets and showers. The wheat field has been replaced by a wildflower meadow and a pond, beside which a bird hide has been built, while the grazing land is now a camping area. A car park has been added between the trees in the north-west and Country Road. Finally, a nature trail now leads down the western side of the site, runs alongside the stream and goes back up on the eastern side.
samples.why: Clear overview · features presented logically in time order · good range of linking · appropriate vocabulary (adapted, preserved) · mostly accurate with a minor tense shift.

samples.text:
The maps show Hollin Farm in 2005 and the same site in 2024, following its conversion into an eco-park. The essential shift has been from agriculture to recreation and conservation, with fields and farm buildings repurposed, although the framework of the site, namely the roads, farmhouse, stream and woodland, remains exactly as before.

The farmhouse still sits in the north, reached by a short road from Country Road, and the cluster of trees to its west has been kept. The two former farm buildings to the east have both been given new functions: the barn now serves as a visitor centre, while the cattle shed has been converted into toilets and showers. A small car park has also been laid out just south of Country Road, alongside the trees.

The greatest changes are to the farmland itself. The western wheat field has been partly transformed into a wildflower meadow, with the remainder of the field given over to a pond overlooked by a bird hide. To the east, the grazing land has become a camping area. These areas are now framed by a nature trail, which descends the western side of the site, follows the stream and climbs back up the eastern side.
samples.why: Sharp overview · changes skilfully selected and precisely located · excellent cohesion (the former, the remainder) · precise, varied vocabulary (repurposed, given over, framed) · wide range of structures, error-free.
